channel.title: Daily Digest
channel.description: Curated tech blog summaries, inspired by Andrej Karpathy's reading list

item.title: Futurism Is Always Extreme
item.description: The article explores the idea that deep, rigorous contemplation of future trends inevitably leads to extreme scenarios. It suggests that moderate visions of the future often fail to capture the radical nature of technological and societal evolution.

item.title: What is the quality of software that AI writes?
item.description: This article explores the debate surrounding the quality of AI-generated code and its future role in software development. It contrasts the perspective that source code may become obsolete with the belief that human oversight remains essential for quality assurance.

item.title: Junk solutions
item.description: This article explores the concept of 'junk solutions' in differential equations, where a mathematical solution lacks physical meaning or relevance. The author discusses how specific families of functions, such as orthogonal polynomials, arise from these equations and notes the importance of distinguishing meaningful results from extraneous mathematical outputs.

item.title: Ultraspherical
item.description: The article discusses the confusing and non-intuitive nature of mathematical terminology, specifically focusing on the term 'ultraspherical polynomials.' It notes that while the prefix 'ultra-' suggests an extreme degree of sphericity, the mathematical definition does not align with this common linguistic interpretation.

item.title: Why didn’t the Windows Entertainment Pack just run the MS-DOS version inside an emulator?
item.description: This post explains that the Windows Entertainment Pack was intended to be a native Windows product rather than a collection of emulated MS-DOS games. It emphasizes the importance of software fitting the platform's specific user experience requirements.

item.title: If your VS Code remotes stopped working, downgrade to v1.124.x
item.description: The author advises users experiencing issues with VS Code remotes to downgrade to version 1.124.x. This quick technical tip addresses recent software regressions affecting remote development workflows.

item.title: How to make VS Code go back to the old UI
item.description: This article discusses the frustration with recent VS Code interface updates and provides a guide or context on reverting to the legacy UI. It highlights the recurring issue of software developers removing user-preferred customization options in favor of mandated design changes.

item.title: Gadget Review: Thermal Master P3 Macro Lens ★★★★⯪
item.description: This review evaluates the Thermal Master P3, a unique thermal camera specifically designed for electronics diagnostics. Unlike standard wildlife-focused thermal cameras, the P3 features a manual macro lens that allows users to capture detailed heat maps of microchips and internal components.

item.title: Pluralistic: The age of disinvention (25 Aug 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow examines the historical battle between media corporations and the VCR, arguing that its eventual decline was a result of intentional industry interference rather than simple technological obsolescence. He highlights the significance of the 1984 Betamax decision, which established that technologies with substantial non-infringing uses are legally protected.

item.title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
item.description: Simon Willison explores Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, a new multimodal mixture-of-experts model that serves as an architectural preview for Qwen4. The post highlights his hands-on experience using quantized versions of the model on a DGX Spark to generate high-quality, complex images.

item.title: Quoting Paul Dix
item.description: This post highlights Paul Dix's perspective on the transformative power of AI in software development. It argues that with proper verification systems and direction, AI can successfully build and refine highly complex, reliable software.

item.title: EVE Online: The Move to Python 3 Begins!
item.description: EVE Online is beginning the massive task of migrating 2.4 million lines of legacy Stackless Python 2.7 code to Python 3. The transition involves automated tools like 'futurize' combined with extensive manual code reviews to address behavioral differences between versions.

item.title: Forgejo hack: How to set a starting issue and pull request number
item.description: The author explores a method for migrating GitHub projects to a self-hosted Forgejo instance by manually adjusting issue and pull request numbering. By modifying the database directly, the author ensures new Forgejo issues start at a specific number to avoid collisions with legacy GitHub identifiers.

item.title: Actually good advice
item.description: This article explores the nuances of social feedback, emphasizing that even well-intentioned advice can be destructive if poorly delivered. It advocates for a more thoughtful approach to interpersonal interactions to avoid unnecessary conflict and hurt feelings.

item.title: Extending life perception
item.description: The author argues that journaling and seeking novel experiences can extend our perception of life by making years feel longer and more memorable. By actively documenting events and breaking routines, we can combat the sensation that time flies, effectively creating a more vivid and lengthened life experience.

item.title: A Cautionary Tale About Data Breach Claims, Verification and Carhartt
item.description: This article examines the risks of blindly trusting claims made by cybercriminals regarding data breaches. Using a specific incident involving Carhartt as a case study, it highlights the importance of rigorous verification rather than relying on unverified claims.

item.title: Have You Heard the Good News About Microlighter?
item.description: The author shares their experience integrating 'microlighter,' a lightweight syntax highlighting tool that utilizes the CSS Custom Highlights API. By moving syntax highlighting from DOM manipulation to a CSS-based styling concern, the author achieves a cleaner, more elegant implementation on their blog.

item.title: Dylan Patel – Anthropic & OpenAI will have most of the world’s compute by 2028
item.description: Dylan Patel discusses the rapid centralization of computing power within major AI labs like Anthropic and OpenAI. He projects that these companies will control the vast majority of global compute resources by 2028, driven by the massive scale required for frontier model training.

item.title: A curmudgeon tries a language server
item.description: The author contrasts their traditional, manual coding workflow with the fluid, integrated development experience of Lisp programming. By comparing the two, they highlight the advantages of Lisp's live-coding and hot-swapping capabilities over standard compile-run-debug cycles.

item.title: The Negative Option
item.source: Tedium: The Dull Side of the Internet.
item.description: This article examines the decline of Columbia House, a once-dominant music distribution service that struggled to adapt to digital disruption. It reflects on the company's historical business model and explores how it eventually faded into obsolescence after failing to pivot successfully in a changing media landscape.

item.title: Hardening the Override Flag
item.description: This article examines how command-line tools and package managers protect against dangerous operations by hardening override flags. It highlights strategies like using verbose, explicit flag names to serve as intentional warnings during security reviews.

item.title: Numerical (in)stability of recurrence relations
item.description: This article discusses the numerical stability challenges inherent in using three-term recurrence relations for special functions. It emphasizes that while these relations are computationally useful, they require careful implementation to avoid errors.

item.title: Comparing the two holograms on the Windows 95 box
item.description: This post examines the subtle differences between the two holographic stickers found on the original Windows 95 retail packaging. The author invites readers to look closely at the design variations present on these collectible boxes.

item.title: Theatre Review: Cats at Regent's Park Open Air Theatre ★★★★☆
item.description: This review of the 'Cats' production at Regent's Park Open Air Theatre critiques the show as a whimsical, spiritual experience. The author draws an anthropological parallel between the performers' feline portrayals and ancient shamanistic rituals of becoming one with an animal.

item.title: Uranium from Příbram (Czechia)
item.description: This post showcases geological specimens of uraninite collected from Příbram, Czechia, featuring radiation measurements and photographic observations. It includes brief technical details on the mineral's formation age and the geological environment of the deposit.

item.title: Foot Guns for Sale
item.source: Software and Tech stories from an Insider - iDiallo.com
item.description: The author challenges the narrative that AI will remain centralized under major providers like OpenAI and Anthropic. Instead, they argue that technological advancements will enable developers to run powerful, open-source models locally, disrupting the current corporate ecosystem model.

item.title: Debugging Ubiquiti's 5G Backup on AT&T
item.description: Jeff Geerling explores integrating Ubiquiti networking gear into a portable 5G mini-homelab rack setup. He highlights the benefits of using compact hardware for both on-the-go connectivity and fixed-location internet redundancy.

item.title: Weekly Update 518: IoT Doorlock Nirvana with UniFi
item.description: Troy Hunt shares his successful implementation of an IoT-based door lock system using Ubiquiti's UniFi platform. The post outlines the key design principles, including the importance of a reliable power source, for integrating smart locks into a residential home.

item.title: distributed identity
item.description: This article explores the challenges of managing contributor identity in Git when personal details like emails and names change over time. It highlights the limitations of git mailmap and proposes using the AT Protocol as a potential solution for managing distributed identity.

item.title: Getting an LLM to Make Me a Tool for Enriching the Color Metadata in My Icon Collection
item.description: The author outlines a workflow for using an LLM to assist in tagging icon metadata by color. Instead of letting the AI decide, he creates a tool that generates color-based recommendations, allowing him to verify and approve the final categorization manually.

item.title: Three-term recurrences
item.description: This article explores three-term recurrence formulas, which are mathematical sequences where each term is a linear combination of the two preceding terms. It highlights the ubiquity of these formulas across various function families and notes the existence of theorems defining their underlying conditions.

item.title: The von Mises-Fisher distribution
item.description: This article discusses the von Mises-Fisher distribution, focusing on the importance of identifying the kernel of a probability density function by ignoring the normalizing constant. It provides insight into the mathematical structure of probability distributions and how they are normalized to integrate to one.

item.title: Anger, Anxiety and Agency
item.description: The author discusses the distinction between anger and anxiety within the tech industry, particularly regarding the rapid evolution of AI. He argues that while anxiety is a natural response to uncertainty, misplaced anger at work is unproductive and suggests focusing on individual agency instead.

item.title: Why do audience members choose specific shows at the Edinburgh Fringe?
item.description: This post examines the lack of audience research conducted by performers at the Edinburgh Fringe despite the significant financial investment required to participate. The author argues that performers are failing to understand their target market, which is crucial for recouping the high costs of staging a production.

item.title: Pluralistic: How Canada can help Americans and defeat America (23 Aug 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: This article examines the volatile nature of US-Canada trade relations under Donald Trump, highlighting the repetitive cycle of ripping up trade deals and imposing tariffs. Doctorow argues that Trump's approach centers on reneging on established agreements, which ultimately harms both Canadian exporters and American consumers.

item.title: llm-anthropic 0.27
item.description: Simon Willison has released llm-anthropic 0.27 to ensure compatibility with the updated Anthropic Python SDK v1.0.0. The update highlights the shift to httpx2 and demonstrates the use of AI tools to automate library migration tasks.

item.title: Your executable is a SQLite database
item.description: Farid Zakaria explores a novel Linux technique that allows a SQLite database file to function as an executable binary. By utilizing the SQLite application ID and specific schema mappings, the file can be interpreted as an ELF executable via a custom loader and binfmt_misc registration.

item.title: The summer of open weights
item.description: The article highlights the rapid advancement of open-weight models in 2026, marking a shift in the AI landscape. It argues that compute availability, rather than model performance, has become the primary driver of market pricing.

item.title: Welcoming the Sri Lankan Government to Have I Been Pwned
item.description: The Sri Lankan government has become the 48th nation to join Have I Been Pwned's free service for government agencies. By integrating with Sri Lanka CERT, the platform enables the government to monitor and respond to data breaches involving official domains.

item.title: Fixing an eMachines EL1200 BIOS bug with Claude
item.description: The author shares their experience using AI to resolve a BIOS bug on an eMachines EL1200, building on their history of hacking legacy hardware. The piece highlights how modern LLMs can assist in troubleshooting complex firmware and technical configuration issues.

item.title: A Syncthing and SQLite Gotcha
item.description: This post explains the technical risks associated with using Syncthing to synchronize SQLite databases. It highlights how the 'rename' system call can lead to data corruption when file synchronization conflicts with database write operations.

item.title: Vim's UserGettingBored autocmd
item.description: This article explores the history and function of Vim's 'UserGettingBored' autocmd, a long-standing joke hidden within the text editor's documentation. While the event itself does not perform any native function, it has persisted for over two decades and eventually inspired a third-party plugin.

item.title: What exactly is modified about a modified Bessel function?
item.description: This article explores the naming conventions of mathematical functions, specifically focusing on why certain Bessel functions are labeled as "modified." It aims to provide context and motivation behind these terms to help readers better understand their mathematical purpose.

item.title: Why special function terminology is arcane
item.description: Special function terminology remains arcane largely due to multiple independent discoveries of the same functions throughout history. This leads to inconsistent notations and definitions as different researchers developed their own conventions for widely useful mathematical tools.

item.title: The difference orbit inclination makes
item.description: This article discusses the importance of accounting for orbital inclination when calculating the distance between planets like Earth and Mars. It explains that while simplified planar models are often used, incorporating the 1.85° tilt of Mars's orbit significantly improves the accuracy of spatial distance measurements.

item.title: Death to px, long live ch!
item.description: The article explains why 'pixels' in CSS are an abstract unit rather than a reflection of physical display hardware. It advocates for using relative units like 'ch' to create more flexible and responsive web layouts.

item.title: Anthropic’s best AI model struggles to attract users as cheaper tools thrive
item.description: This post analyzes current financial and adoption trends for Anthropic and OpenAI based on recent reports and billing data. It highlights that while Anthropic is seeing revenue growth, its most expensive models are struggling to gain traction compared to more cost-effective alternatives.

item.title: Quoting Drew Breunig
item.description: Drew Breunig reflects on how the arrival of expensive, high-performance models like Fable signals the end of relying on constantly improving, cheap AI to fix coding inefficiencies. This shift forces developers to be more strategic about which model is used for specific tasks to optimize costs.

item.title: My agent.md to improve LLM-assisted code quality
item.description: This article discusses the use of an 'agent.md' file as a structured approach to enhance code quality when working with Large Language Models. It likely provides a framework for guiding LLM interactions to ensure better output consistency and maintainability.

item.title: Concurrent Servers: Part 8 - Go
item.description: This article is the eighth installment in a series exploring concurrent network server implementations, focusing specifically on the Go programming language. It demonstrates how to build a sequential state-machine server in Go, providing code examples to illustrate the process.

item.title: Reading List 08/22/26
item.description: This post provides a curated list of readings covering diverse infrastructure and housing topics, including Los Angeles' ADU trends, electrical manufacturing, and energy production. It also touches on water resource management in the Colorado River basin.

item.title: This Week in Package Management: 22 August 2026
item.description: This roundup highlights key updates in package management for the week, including Go 1.27's refined module handling and Rust 1.98's new crate publishing filters. It also covers the release of Bun 1.4, which features a transition to a Rust-based codebase, and updates to pnpm's installation and lockfile performance.

item.title: Coming soon
item.description: The author uses a local 'Coming Soon' pizza shop sign to explore the mathematical modeling of wait times for future events. He discusses how to estimate the time until a specific event occurs based on observation intervals.

item.title: Fast and Hard Code
item.description: The rise of LLMs has reduced the friction of learning new programming languages, leading developers to prioritize performance and marketing over language familiarity. This trend is fueling the adoption of high-performance, complex languages like Rust and Zig, even when developers lack deep expertise in them.

item.title: Pluralistic: Born on technology's third base (21 Aug 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow reflects on the societal and historical advantages that shaped his tech career, emphasizing how being born in 1971 to supportive parents provided a unique head start. He argues that individual success is often the result of favorable structural conditions rather than personal merit alone.

item.title: Quoting Linus Torvalds
item.description: Linus Torvalds recounts using AI to assist in a difficult Linux kernel debugging session. While the AI provided significant help with grunt work, it frequently suggested giving up, highlighting the necessity of human persistence in complex problem-solving.

item.title: llm 0.33
item.description: Simon Willison released version 0.33 of his LLM CLI tool, featuring an upgrade to the OpenAI Python library and support for per-call keys in embedding methods. Additionally, the update enables the chaining of multiple templates to combine model configurations and prompt instructions.

item.title: More than just code review
item.description: The author argues that effectively using coding agents requires more than just traditional line-by-line code review. He suggests that developers should shift their focus toward better verification methods to ensure AI-generated changes are accurate and reliable.

item.title: You should never be angry at work
item.description: This article discusses the professional and personal drawbacks of expressing anger in the workplace. It advocates for emotional regulation and maintaining composure to preserve one's reputation and long-term career success.

item.title: Why shaming people about AI slop isn’t enough to stop Big AI
item.description: Anil Dash argues that shaming AI usage is insufficient to counter the influence of Big AI corporations. He suggests that the current binary narrative, which frames the choice as either using exploitative AI tools or nothing at all, ignores viable alternatives and fails to challenge the systemic power of tech giants.

item.title: A Need for Speed
item.description: The author reflects on their youth as a car enthusiast, sharing personal anecdotes about their first vehicle, a 1966 Volkswagen Beetle. This nostalgic piece serves as a reflective introduction to the author's history with mechanical interests.

item.title: Rust Glancer
item.description: The author discusses Rust Glancer, a memory-efficient LSP server for Rust, while critiquing current syntax tree approaches in tools like rust-analyzer. The post highlights the challenges of indexing large workspaces and suggests potential optimizations for function analysis and proc macro handling.

item.title: How would you know whether an ancient culture had zero?
item.description: The article explores the mathematical requirements for a number system to include a concept of zero, using spreadsheet column labels as a comparative example. It highlights the distinction between positional notation systems with and without a zero placeholder.

item.title: Reducing C++ template bloat by factoring out the type-dependent portions of the function, practical exam
item.description: This article discusses practical strategies for reducing C++ template bloat by identifying and isolating type-dependent code. It emphasizes refactoring techniques that minimize binary size while maintaining template functionality.

item.title: Reducing C++ template bloat by factoring out the type-dependent portions of the function
item.description: This post discusses techniques for optimizing C++ code by minimizing template bloat. It recommends identifying and separating type-dependent code to consolidate function implementations.

item.title: Book Review: An Immense World - How Animal Senses Reveal the Hidden Realms Around Us by Ed Yong ★★★☆☆
item.description: This book review explores Ed Yong's 'An Immense World,' which examines the diverse and often alien sensory perceptions of the animal kingdom. The author highlights how the book moves beyond simple comparisons to provide a deeper understanding of how different species experience their environments.

item.title: Pluralistic: The actual epistemic crisis (20 Aug 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow argues that AI is fueling an 'epistemic crisis' by democratizing the creation of realistic deepfakes, making it impossible to discern truth from fabrication. He compares this phenomenon to Vladislav Surkov’s strategy of sowing universal doubt, which erodes trust in reality itself.

item.title: llm 0.32.1
item.description: Simon Willison released version 0.32.1 of the LLM tool to resolve a dependency issue caused by changes in the OpenAI Python library. The update pins the library version to ensure stability while preparing for a migration to httpx2 in the next release.

item.title: llm-openrouter 0.7
item.description: Simon Willison has released llm-openrouter 0.7, featuring compatibility with LLM 0.32 and support for OpenRouter's Responses API. The update also introduces three new server-side tools: Shell, WebFetch, and WebSearch.

item.title: Stop Making TUIs
item.description: Thomas Ptacek argues that developers should stop relying solely on command-line interfaces for personal projects, as coding agents now make creating native GUIs trivial. Simon Willison supports this perspective, noting that leveraging AI tools like LLMs can quickly turn throwaway scripts into functional desktop applications.

item.title: Quoting Matt Webb
item.description: Matt Webb discusses using ChatGPT as an interactive tutor to master complex mathematical concepts like quaternions for app development. He emphasizes that AI does not replace human learning but rather serves as a catalyst for deeper understanding and skill acquisition.

item.title: ChatGPT search now uses the site:operator at scale
item.description: Promptwatch data reveals that ChatGPT has significantly increased its use of site-specific search operators, likely tied to recent updates in its underlying search engine technology. The analysis highlights the emergence of Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) as a critical practice for brands to track visibility in AI chatbot responses.

item.title: A shot-scraper-style JSON API on Bun 1.4's new Bun.WebView
item.description: Simon Willison explores the new Bun.WebView feature released in Bun 1.4, which enables native browser automation. He demonstrates how to leverage this capability to build a JSON API similar to his shot-scraper tool.

item.title: Readers can't identify watermarked AI text
item.description: This article explores the limitations of watermarking technology in identifying AI-generated text. It highlights that current methods often fail to reliably detect machine-written content, raising concerns about the efficacy of AI labeling.

item.title: Introducing Dashboard Touch, a build-your-own version of Touch ID
item.description: Anil Dash introduces Dashboard Touch, an open-source project that allows users to build a custom external fingerprint sensor for Mac. By utilizing low-cost hardware and a user-friendly web interface, the project provides a functional alternative to Apple's integrated Touch ID.

item.title: A Sloppy Interface Is a Security Liability ￼
item.description: This post argues that high-quality, professional interface design serves as a vital security control against phishing and brand impersonation. As AI makes it trivial to replicate low-effort interfaces, the author warns that maintaining sloppy design habits creates vulnerabilities that bad actors can easily exploit.

item.title: Our Servants Will Do That For Us
item.description: This article explores the skepticism surrounding the realization of a post-scarcity utopia. It argues that societal and economic structures make such a vision unlikely, challenging the optimistic assumptions often associated with technological abundance.

item.title: Issues in the Repo
item.description: This article discusses the fragility of relying solely on GitHub for project issue tracking and review data. It explores various decentralized alternatives that store issue data directly within the git repository, analyzing their different approaches to data modeling and synchronization.

item.title: Better Batteries
item.description: The author argues that the quality of a programming language's standard library depends on social and institutional architecture rather than its size. Comparing Python, Go, and Rust, the post highlights how organizational capacity dictates the long-term success and consistency of standard libraries.

item.title: AI-generated ASCII diagrams
item.description: The article explores the unexpected use of modern AI models to generate retro 1970s-style ASCII diagrams. It highlights the aesthetic appeal of this incongruity while noting practical benefits, such as significantly smaller file sizes compared to traditional image formats.

item.title: On wrapping a callable in a lambda that just calls it with the same parameters
item.description: This post advises against wrapping a callable in a lambda when the lambda simply passes the same arguments to the original function. It recommends using the callable directly to keep code cleaner and more efficient.

item.title: smolmachines / smolvm as a sandbox for untrusted Python & JavaScript
item.description: Simon Willison documents an experiment using Claude Code to evaluate 'smolmachines' as a secure sandbox for untrusted code execution. Since the environment lacked nested virtualization, the process shifted to using GitHub Actions to perform real-world testing of resource-constrained Python and JavaScript execution.

item.title: Quoting Jeremy Morrell
item.description: Jeremy Morrell proposes that Large Language Models and modern sandboxing technologies make it easier and safer to build extensible software. By using LLMs to generate extensions, developers can create core applications that users can safely customize and enhance.

item.title: Conceptual integrity and counting lines of code
item.description: Simon Willison discusses how AI agents challenge traditional software development metrics by enabling significantly higher code output. He argues that while lines of code can now be a valid productivity indicator, the true constraint for development has shifted from raw coding speed to human cognitive capacity.

item.title: Getting the Steam Deck LCD working on a Raspberry Pi
item.description: Jeff Geerling explores using the affordable Steam Deck LCD screen for Raspberry Pi projects. By utilizing a new Linux kernel driver developed by Scandent, this higher-resolution screen becomes a superior alternative to the official Raspberry Pi display.

item.title: Good writing is obvious, not original
item.description: This article argues that effective writing prioritizes clarity and accessibility over the pursuit of radical originality. It suggests that clear communication of existing ideas is more valuable than striving for novelty.

item.title: Big little hexagon
item.description: This article discusses a recent research paper regarding the maximum-area polygon problem for a given number of sides and a diameter of one. It highlights the surprising geometric findings, noting that while regular polygons are optimal for odd numbers of sides, the pattern for even sides is more complex.

item.title: What Is Reasoning
item.description: This article explores the technical nature of AI 'reasoning traces,' explaining that they are simply text generated in a scratchpad area rather than a mysterious internal process. It clarifies that these traces are managed through specific response formats and system prompts rather than being fundamental properties of the sampling process.

item.title: Why did the Microsoft Entertainment Pack for Windows have a special sticker announcing that it also had Tetris?
item.description: This post explains the historical reason behind a special sticker on the Microsoft Entertainment Pack for Windows. It reveals that the prominent inclusion of Tetris was a contingency plan to ensure the package's market appeal.

item.title: Anubis continues to expose new ways people configure webservers
item.description: This post highlights how web server administrators often unintentionally break website functionality by disabling browser features. It emphasizes the importance of understanding the side effects of configuration changes to avoid difficult debugging scenarios.

item.title: Asymmetric Agents
item.description: The post explores the concept of 'asymmetric agents' in AI, critiquing the long-standing industry trope of autonomous personal digital servants. It highlights the practical difficulties and underlying power dynamics involved in delegating complex negotiations and tasks to AI agents.

item.title: Pluralistic: The ordinariness of evil (19 Aug 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow argues that the exaggerated 'existential risk' narratives surrounding AI are marketing strategies meant to boost the perceived potential of products that currently function only as niche tools. He positions AI as a mundane technology, suggesting its actual utility is marginal and often overshadowed by the hype surrounding its development.

item.title: Hands-on with Raspberry Pi's CM5 Programming Jig
item.description: Jeff Geerling explores the Raspberry Pi CM5 Programming Jig as a solution for streamlining the tedious process of flashing multiple Compute Modules. The post highlights the difficulty of managing mass deployments and how specialized hardware can simplify device configuration.

item.title: I like 'em thick
item.description: The author reflects on their evolving relationship with writing, moving from an obsession with conciseness to a newfound appreciation for density and length. They argue that verbose prose can offer deeper engagement and stylistic richness, challenging the conventional academic emphasis on brevity.

item.title: Weekly Update 517: Cyber Ransoms
item.description: This update explores the evolving landscape of ransomware, highlighting that much of the activity is driven by extortion rather than traditional software-based locking. It discusses the challenges young cybercriminals face when attempting to launder and spend their illicit gains.

item.title: my-personsal-agi
item.description: This article discusses the concept of personal AGI, exploring what it means to develop or utilize artificial general intelligence at an individual level. It examines the potential implications and personal applications of such technology.

item.title: AI Alignment as a Thought-Terminating Cliche
item.description: This piece critiques the term 'AI alignment' as a thought-terminating cliché that simplifies complex sociotechnical problems. It argues that the phrase is often used rhetorically to bypass critical inquiry into the actual mechanics and implications of AI safety.

item.title: Vim wants you to control, VSCode wants you to consume
item.description: The author compares the configuration philosophies of VSCode and Neovim, highlighting how VSCode focuses on consuming predefined commands while Neovim emphasizes controlling editor state through executable code. This reflection is sparked by the author's transition to a new role at Antithesis, where they are adopting NixOS and reconsidering their complex editor setup.

item.title: Snakes and Ladders
item.description: The article discusses the common use of themed 'Snakes and Ladders' board games in promotional material for children. It reflects on why these games are effective marketing tools by tapping into a child's imagination as they navigate the board.

item.title: Two-Factor Authentication Across Package Registries
item.description: This article examines the progress of two-factor authentication (2FA) implementation across major package registries. It highlights how different registries, such as npm and PyPI, are navigating the transition to mandatory security measures to close account-bypass vulnerabilities.
